about: A music take with `out: null` is kept as a raw take only (not in the game); `out` names where the chosen take goes. Every generated sound and piece of music: its prompt, how it is cut, and where it goes. `node scripts/sound/make.mjs` turns this into public/sound (see README.md). Seed Audio speaks a prompt unless it starts with 'The sound of'.

music.prompt: An epic and hopeful title theme for a game set a thousand years in the future inside a vast O'Neill cylinder habitat in Earth orbit. Starts quiet and spacious with glass bells and soft high strings, slowly builds to a broad, warm, uplifting climax with wordless choir, full strings, low brass and a gentle electronic pulse, then settles into calm wonder. Orchestral with a folk warmth. Instrumental, no lyrics.

An epic and hopeful title theme for a game about a gentle, thoughtful civilisation living in giant rotating space habitats a thousand years from now. Hybrid of warm analogue synthesizers and live strings, a steady rising arpeggio, swelling pads and a soaring melody that opens like a sunrise, ending in quiet awe. Instrumental, no lyrics.

An epic and hopeful title theme with a future-folk character for a game set inside a vast space habitat full of forests, rivers and people who make things by hand. A solo acoustic instrument and wordless voice open alone, then hand drums, strings and a big warm ensemble join and lift into a joyful, wide climax, then return to the single voice. Instrumental, no lyrics.

An epic and hopeful title theme called First Light, for a game set a thousand years from now among giant rotating space habitats in orbit around Earth. It opens out of near silence: for the first ten seconds only single, high, glassy notes appear one by one like stars coming out, over a very low warm swell. At about twelve seconds the main theme enters: a clear, memorable, singable melody of a few notes that rises like a sunrise. It is stated first by a solo French horn over soft strings, then taken up by the full orchestra with timpani and low brass in a broad, uplifting climax, and finally returns to the lone horn and the glassy star notes, ending in quiet awe. Instrumental only: no vocals, no choir, no voices, no lyrics.
